extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO staff/examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules for timely filing of correspondence (certificate of mailing/transmission; Priority Mail Express), petitions to accord filing dates, public access to application/patent files and reexamination/PTAB files, assignment-records access, and rules on copies and confidentiality of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension when deadline falls on weekend or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: If the day that is twelve months after the filing date of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) falls on Saturday, Sunday, or on a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the period of pendency shall be extended to the next succeeding secular or business day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 90.3 of this chapter for time for appeal or for commencing civil action. (Applies to specified statutory time periods; additional citations and revision history included.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing or transmission — general rule for timely filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence required to be filed in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office within a set period of time will be considered as being timely filed if the procedure described in this section is followed. The actual date of receipt will be used for all other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence will be considered timely filed if mailed or transmitted prior to expiration of the period by being (A) addressed as set out in § 1.1(a) and deposited with the U.S. Postal Service with sufficient postage as first class mail; (B) transmitted by facsimile to the Patent and Trademark Office in accordance with § 1.6(d); or (C) transmitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system in accordance with § 1.6(a)(4). Each piece must include a certificate stating the date of deposit or transmission, and the person signing should have a reasonable basis to expect that the correspondence would be mailed or transmitted on or before the date indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing/transmission — explicit exclusions (no benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate-of-mailing/transmission procedure does not apply to certain filings and no benefit will be given to a Certificate of Mailing or Transmission on specified categories of papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated exclusions include: filings to obtain an application filing date (including CPA requests under § 1.53(d)); papers filed in PTAB trials governed by § 42.6(b) (or § 41.106(f) as applicable); filing of an international application for patent; filing correspondence in an international application before U.S. Receiving Office/ISA/IPEA; filing a copy of the international application and basic national fee to enter the national stage (§ 1.495(b)); filing a written declaration of abandonment under § 1.138; filing under § 1.217 for publication of a redacted copy; third-party submissions under § 1.290; calculation of any period of adjustment (§ 1.703(f)); filing of an international design application; correspondence in disciplinary proceedings under part 11. (The rule lists specific subparagraphs (A)-(K) etc.)

rubrics_metrics.name: If correspondence appears timely mailed/transmitted but Office has no evidence — remedial steps
rubrics_metrics.description: When correspondence is considered timely filed by being mailed or transmitted per paragraph (a) but not received by the USPTO after a reasonable time, or the application is held abandoned or proceeding dismissed, the correspondence will be considered timely if the party who forwarded it complies with specified steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required actions: (1) inform the Office promptly after becoming aware that the Office has no evidence of receipt; (2) supply an additional copy of the previously mailed or transmitted correspondence and certificate; and (3) include a statement that attests on personal knowledge basis or to the satisfaction of the Director to the previous timely mailing, transmission or submission. For facsimile, a copy of the sending unit’s transmission report may be used; for USPTO e-filing, an acknowledgment receipt may be used. The Office may require additional evidence to determine timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express® filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correspondence received by the USPTO that was delivered by the Priority Mail Express® Post Office to Addressee service of the USPS will be considered filed with the USPTO on the date of deposit with the USPS, as shown by the 'date accepted' on the Priority Mail Express® label or other official USPS notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPS deposit date cannot be determined, the correspondence will be accorded the USPTO receipt date as the filing date. Correspondence should be deposited directly with a USPS employee to ensure receipt of a legible 'date accepted' label; deposit in a drop box is at the sender's risk. The Priority Mail Express® mailing label number should be placed on the paper(s) or fee(s) that constitute the correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to Director — discrepancy between USPTO filing date and USPS 'date accepted'
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can show a discrepancy between the filing date accorded by the Office and the 'date accepted' on the Priority Mail Express® label may petition the Director to accord the correspondence the USPS deposit date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) filed promptly after becoming aware of the discrepancy; (2) the Priority Mail Express® mailing label number was placed on the papers or fees prior to mailing; and (3) the petition includes a true copy of the Priority Mail Express® mailing label showing the 'date accepted' and any other official USPS notation relied upon to show the date of deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when 'date accepted' incorrectly entered or omitted by USPS
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can show that the 'date accepted' on the Priority Mail Express® mailing label or other official notation entered by the USPS was incorrectly entered or omitted may petition the Director to accord the correspondence a filing date of the actual deposit date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) filed promptly after awareness; (2) label number placed on papers or fees prior to original mailing; and (3) petition includes a showing establishing, to the satisfaction of the Director, that the requested filing date was the date deposited in Priority Mail Express® prior to the last scheduled pickup for that day. Any showing must be corroborated by evidence from the USPS or evidence created after deposit and within one business day of deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when Priority Mail Express® correspondence not received by USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: A person whose Priority Mail Express® correspondence addressed per § 1.1(a) and mailed with sufficient postage was not received may petition the Director to consider the correspondence filed on the USPS deposit date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) filed promptly after awareness that Office has no evidence of receipt; (2) label number placed on papers or fees prior to mailing; (3) includes a copy of the originally deposited papers or fees showing the label number, copy of any returned postcard receipt, copy of the Priority Mail Express® mailing label showing 'date accepted', copy of any other official USPS notation relied upon; and (4) includes a statement establishing to Director's satisfaction the original deposit and that provided copies are true copies. If requested filing date differs from 'date accepted', include showing pursuant to paragraph (d)(3). The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when correspondence returned due to interruption or emergency in Priority Mail Express® service
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence was returned by USPS due to an interruption or emergency in Priority Mail Express® service, the sender may petition the Director to consider such correspondence filed on a particular date in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include a statement establishing to the Director's satisfaction the original deposit and that the correspondence or copy is the original or a true copy of the originally deposited correspondence. The Office may require additional evidence to determine if return was due to interruption or emergency in service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when deposit was refused by USPS employee due to interruption/emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a USPS employee refused to accept correspondence (Priority Mail Express®) due to an interruption or emergency in service, a petition may be filed to have the correspondence considered filed on a particular date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (1) petition filed promptly after awareness of refusal; (2) label number placed on papers or fees prior to attempted mailing; (3) petition includes original correspondence or copy showing the mailing label number; and (4) petition includes a statement by the person who originally attempted deposit establishing the attempt and that the correspondence or copy is original or true copy. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require additional evidence for Priority Mail Express® matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require additional evidence to determine if correspondence was deposited as Priority Mail Express® with the USPS on the date in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across petitions involving Priority Mail Express® deposit date discrepancies, incorrect entries, non-receipt, returns, or refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files open to the public — published applications, patents, and statutory invention registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification, drawings, and all papers relating to the file of: a published application; a patent; or a statutory invention registration are open to inspection by the public, and copies may be obtained upon payment of the fee set forth in § 1.19(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application was published in redacted form under § 1.217, the complete file wrapper and contents will not be available if the § 1.217 requirements have been met and the application is still pending. See § 2.27 for trademark files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue applications and opened-compl ete-application requests — public access and Official Gazette announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications, all applications in which the Office has accepted a request to open the complete application to inspection by the public, and related papers in the application file, are open to inspection and copies may be furnished upon fee payment; filing of reissue applications will be announced in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Gazette announcement shall include at least: filing date, reissue application and original patent numbers, title, class and subclass, inventor name, owner of record, attorney or agent of record, and examining group assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination announcements and public access to reexamination records
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for reexamination satisfying § 1.510 or § 1.915 will be announced in the Official Gazette; Director-initiated reexaminations under § 1.520 will also be announced. Papers or copies entered of record in the patent or reexamination file are open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements shall include at least the date of request, reexamination request control number or Director order control number, patent number, title, class/subclass, inventor, patent owner of record, and examining group to which reexamination is assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB interference or trial files — public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as prohibited in § 41.6(b), § 42.14 or § 42.410(b), the file of any interference or trial before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board is open to public inspection and copies of the file may be obtained upon payment of the fee therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain exceptions referenced in parts 41 and 42 limit access where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment records — maintenance and public access for patents and trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate assignment records are maintained in the USPTO for patents and trademarks. Assignment records (including digests and indexes for assignments recorded on or after May 1, 1957) and published patent applications are open to public inspection and copies obtainable upon request and payment of the fee set forth in § 1.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment records for patents recorded before May 1, 1957 are maintained by NARA and are open to public inspection; certified and uncertified copies provided by NARA upon request and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment records for pending or abandoned applications — access limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment records, digests, and indexes relating to any pending or abandoned patent application that is open to the public pursuant to § 1.11 or for which copies/access may be supplied pursuant to § 1.14 are available to the public. Assignment records not available to the public are obtainable only upon written authority or upon a showing of bona fide interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written authority must be from an inventor, the applicant, the assignee or assignee of an undivided part interest, or a patent practitioner of record; alternatively, a showing that the requester is a bona fide prospective/actual purchaser, mortgagee, or licensee, or necessary to proper conduct of business before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for assignment records preserved in confidence — petition or written authority required
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request by a member of the public seeking copies of assignment records of any pending or abandoned patent application preserved in confidence under § 1.14 must either be in the form of a petition including the fee set forth in § 1.17(g) or include written authority granting access from the inventor/applicant/assignee or practitioner of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure ensures protected/confidential assignment records are disclosed only with proper authorization or by petition and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering assignment copies — identify reel and frame number
rubrics_metrics.description: An order for a copy of an assignment or other document should identify the reel and frame number where the assignment or document is recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a document is identified without specifying correct reel and frame, an extra charge as set forth in § 1.21(j) will be made for time consumed in making a search for such assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and certified copies — availability and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-certified copies of patents, patent application publications, and records under USPTO jurisdiction and open to the public will be furnished to any person upon payment of appropriate fee. Certified copies of patents, application publications, and trademark registrations and records will be authenticated by the USPTO seal and certified by the Director upon payment of the certified copy fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to applicable fee sections (§ 1.19 and § 2.201 for trademarks) and revision history are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of unpublished patent applications (preserved in confidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning filing, pendency, subject matter, status, and access to the application will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or in § 1.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (a) introduces availability situations (patented applications/statutory invention registrations; published abandoned applications; published pending applications) and notes limits (e.g., redacted copies used for publication may limit what is provided; Office will not provide access to paper file of a pending published application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i)). Further provisions for international and design applications appear in subsequent paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of records in specified situations (patented, published abandoned, published pending applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records associated with patent applications may be available in the following situations: (i) issued patents or statutory invention registrations (file available as set forth in § 1.11(a)); (ii) published abandoned applications (file available as set forth in § 1.11(a)); (iii) published pending applications (copies of application-as-filed, file contents, or specific documents may be provided upon request and payment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a redacted copy of the application was used for publication under § 1.217, the copy of specification, drawings, and papers may be limited to a redacted copy. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application that has been published, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i) of § 1.14.
